subject: Polity
description: Article 93, election, powers, removal, casting vote, money-bill certification

questions.stem: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected by:

options.option_text: All MPs of both Houses by single transferable vote
Members of the Lok Sabha from amongst themselves
President on advice of the Prime Minister
Council of Ministers by absolute majority vote

questions.explanation: Article 93 — Lok Sabha shall elect a Speaker + Deputy Speaker from amongst its members. Elected by simple majority. Conventionally — Speaker from ruling party, Deputy Speaker from opposition (since 6th LS). Speaker continues even if LS is dissolved, until the new Speaker is elected. Salary + allowances charged on Consolidated Fund of India (Article 112). Distractor 1 — that's how President is elected (with weighted formulae). Distractor 3 — President doesn't appoint. Distractor 4 — Council doesn't elect.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The CASTING VOTE in the Lok Sabha is exercised by:

options.option_text: The Prime Minister, in case of any tie vote
The Speaker, only when there is a tie
The Leader of Opposition, on a tie vote
The President of India in deadlock cases

questions.explanation: Article 100 — Speaker does NOT vote in the first instance. But in case of a TIE (equal votes for and against), Speaker has the CASTING VOTE — the second, deciding vote. This preserves Speaker's appearance of impartiality during normal voting. Same convention in Westminster + most parliaments. Notable use: Vajpayee government fell by 1 vote in 1999 (no-confidence; 269 vs 270, did not require Speaker's casting vote). Distractor 1 — PM is an MP, votes normally. Distractor 3 — LoP has no special vote. Distractor 4 — President doesn't vote in Parliament.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Speaker is REMOVED from office by:

options.option_text: Resolution passed by majority of all members of LS
Direct order of the Prime Minister with cabinet
Joint sitting of both Houses with 2/3 majority
Two-thirds vote of the Supreme Court only

questions.explanation: Article 94 — Speaker can be removed by a RESOLUTION passed by a MAJORITY OF ALL THE THEN MEMBERS of Lok Sabha (effective majority — more than half of total membership, NOT just present + voting). Requires 14-day prior notice. While the resolution is being considered, Deputy Speaker presides. Speaker can speak + vote in such resolution. Other grounds for vacancy: cease to be MP; resignation (to Deputy Speaker). Distractor 2 — PM can't remove. Distractor 3 — joint sitting not the procedure. Distractor 4 — SC doesn't remove the Speaker.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: MONEY BILL certification (whether a bill IS or IS NOT a Money Bill) is done by:

options.option_text: Finance Minister of the central government
Speaker of the Lok Sabha (final decision)
Chairman (Vice-President) of Rajya Sabha
President in consultation with the cabinet

questions.explanation: Article 110(3) — 'If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill, the decision of the SPEAKER of the House of the People shall be final.' Hugely consequential power: Money Bills bypass Rajya Sabha (RS can only recommend; LS can override). Aadhaar Act 2016 was certified as Money Bill by Speaker — controversially, leading to SC rulings. SC has held the Speaker's decision is justiciable on the basis of constitutional interpretation (Rojer Mathew, 2019, referred to larger bench, pending). Distractors are not the certifying authority.

questions.stem: The FIRST Speaker of the Lok Sabha (post-Constitution) was:

options.option_text: G.V. Mavlankar, the 'Father of Lok Sabha'
M.A. Ayyangar, who succeeded Mavlankar later
Sumitra Mahajan, the second woman Speaker
Meira Kumar, the first woman LS Speaker

questions.explanation: G.V. MAVLANKAR — first Speaker of Lok Sabha (15 May 1952 - 27 Feb 1956); died in office. Earlier presided over the Constituent Assembly (Legislative). Called 'FATHER OF LOK SABHA'. Successors: M.A. AYYANGAR (1956-62), Hukam Singh, N. Sanjiva Reddy (later President), G.S. Dhillon, Bali Ram Bhagat. First WOMAN speaker — MEIRA KUMAR (2009-14, daughter of Jagjivan Ram). SUMITRA MAHAJAN was the second woman speaker (2014-19). Current Speaker (Jun 2024-): Om Birla.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the Lok Sabha is dissolved, the Speaker:

options.option_text: Vacates office immediately on dissolution
Continues in office till the new LS is constituted
Becomes acting Prime Minister till elections
Joins the Rajya Sabha as a nominated member

questions.explanation: Speaker continues in office EVEN AFTER dissolution of the Lok Sabha — until the day immediately before the first sitting of the next Lok Sabha. This ensures continuity and that someone can preside if a special session is called between dissolution and the new LS. Speaker's ROLE: presides over LS; maintains discipline; decides points of order; certifies Money Bills; chairs the Joint Sitting of both Houses (Article 108).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Speaker's role under the 10th SCHEDULE (Anti-Defection Law) is to:

options.option_text: Enforce party whip on every parliamentary vote
Decide cases of disqualification of MPs for defection
Suspend defecting members for one full session
Refer defection cases to the Election Commission

questions.explanation: Under 10th Schedule, Speaker (LS) / Chairman (RS) decides disqualification cases for defection. Earlier rulings — Speaker's decision was 'final and not subject to judicial review'. Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1993) — SC held that Speaker's decision IS subject to judicial review (under Articles 136, 226, 227) — but COURT cannot intervene BEFORE the Speaker decides. SC has criticised Speakers for delaying decisions on convenience (Maharashtra 2022, Manipur 2020 — recommended Parliament consider an INDEPENDENT TRIBUNAL).
